jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1Full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of decentralized securityJoin a World-Class Research Team in Information Security The Chair for Information Security at Ruhr University Bochum — led by Prof. Dr. Ghassan Karame and part of the Faculty of Computer Science since 2021 — brings together an international, multicultural team of researchers pushing the boundaries of decentralized and systems security. Our work spans a broad spectrum of security and privacy challenges, with a particular emphasis on decentralized security and distributed machine learning security. We are proud to be affiliated with: • Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI), one of Europe's most respected centers for fundamental research in computer security. Founded over two decades ago, HGI maintains deep collaborations with world-renowned academic institutions, industry leaders, and media partners — and has been a launchpad for numerous successful cybersecurity startups. CASA — Cluster of Excellence: Securing the Digital Society is a leading center for cybersecurity research at Ruhr University Bochum. Through an innovative and interdisciplinary research program, CASA strengthens the resilience of the digital society, bringing together internationally renowned researchers to develop next-generation security solutions that holistically protect large-scale socio-technical systems, spanning cryptography, hardware and software, and the intersection of technology with users and society. Funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) with €53 million for its second phase from 2026 to 2032, CASA is hosted at the Horst Görtz Institute (HGI) at RUB and partnered with the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy (MPI-SP).The Chair for Information Security has an immediate full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of (decentralized) systems security (currently 39.83 hours /week = 100%).Scope: full-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 JahreStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-02Your tasks:- The main task in this position is to research, analyze, and improve the security and privacy of modern decentralized platforms while enhancing their performance and scalability.- Members of Prof. Karame's Chair conduct research and teaching in various areas of IT security. jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for 1Doctoral Position (m,f,x) in Computational Neuroscience (Project Z02)Are you curious about how the human brain stores and retrieves memories? You want bridge the gap between academia and the wider public? The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework which conceptualizes scenarios as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information.We are actively seeking a talented PhD student to join our science communication project within the CRC 1844, which develops a digital serious game for citizen science, establishing a bidirectional bridge between episodic memory (EM) research and the general public. On the one hand, the game facilitates dissemination and intervention studies, with the public being involved in game design and extensions. On the other hand, the game allows for large-scale EM data collection from a diverse population. It also enables longitudinal research on EM, as well as prospective studies of EM changes preceding psychopathology.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)Start: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-02Your tasks:- The primary task will be the analysis of the behavioral data from gamified EM tasks, development of novel analyses, and interpretation of the results- Help adapt laboratory experiments into a serious game setting in collaboration with the Cologne Game Lab- Help validate the collected EM data in collaboration with experimental projects in the CRC 1844- Assist the outreach coordinator associated with this project with player recruitment and outreach activities- Correlate memory performance data from the game with demographic and psychological data in collaboration with the DZPG (German Center for Mental Health)- Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations with experimental and computational neuroscientists, psychologists, and philosophers- Present your results and findings in international conferences and scientific journalsYour profile:- An excellent master’s degree, or equivalent, in computational neuroscience, physics, mathematics, computer science, or a related field- Ability to work independently- Competence in mathematical modeling and statistical analysis- Excellent programming skills, e.g., Python- Relevant research experience in neuroscience or a related field- Excellent communication skills in English- Team spirit- Experience working within a collaborative research group (optional)https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/fec7155cf49f90ef54729f1412129f5b84aed4f70?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/fec7155cf49f90ef54729f1412129f5b84aed4f70?ref=AfA)
